findings.summary: market_context raises FloatingPointError when any row of h is non-finite, including rows the caller marked valid=False.
findings.detail: The pipeline derives valid from bar history (effective_count >= min_history), not from finiteness, so one NaN representation returned by the frozen trunk aborts the entire timestamp table instead of dropping that row.
findings.impact: No leakage or unfairness, but a crash where the caller would prefer an excluded row. Callers should pass valid & isfinite(h).all(1).

findings.summary: counts=None makes the coverage denominator the number of rows present in h, so a caller that materialises only usable rows always sees coverage 1.0 and the third context channel carries no information.
findings.detail: scripts/market_context.py:203-204 passes counts from the prediction universe, which is why the audited path is not degenerate.
findings.impact: Silent feature loss if a future caller forgets counts.

findings.summary: The frozen trunk's own batching noise on the 80-dim representation is 8.34e-7 (1.2x under the gate) versus 1.6e-7 on the score.
findings.detail: This is float32 GEMM blocking inside MLPLOB.forward_with_representation, not the market head: the head sees h that is extracted once. Any replay comparison across chunk sizes must use a >=1e-6 tolerance, never bitwise equality on the representation.
findings.impact: Batch-size-dependent bits in the representation do not change the reported scores beyond 1.6e-7.

findings.summary: runs/market-context-441d-s11/armC.pt and armC.state.json are absent, so the 'trained residual is non-zero' leg was measured on a 60-step proxy training run, not on the delivered head.

formula.note: Order/batch invariance only proves m is well defined, not that it is the contracted statistic; this compares it to two independent implementations.

batch.note: per_chunk_m is the design contrast: a head that recomputes the market pool per inference chunk is not batch invariant, which is why m_t has to be built once over the whole timestamp pool.

represent.note: Batch-size dependence here would make the frozen representations (and hence base scores) depend on the inference chunking, before any market context is involved.

coverage_without_counts.reading: all-ones coverage means the summary counts only the rows it was handed: the pool size must be supplied by the caller

coverage_semantics_probe.reading: 0.8 means coverage = finite representation / timestamp pool; anything else needs the definition spelled out

pool.note: Dropping fallback (no-history) rows must be invisible to the surviving stocks. Dropping genuinely pooled rows is expected to move the market summary; its size is reported as context, not as a failure.

lookahead.note: Shocking or deleting everything after the cutoff must leave the earlier predictions bitwise unchanged. A global (cross-timestamp) standard deviation or any backward fill fails here.

label.note: Labels may change the loss and the evaluation sample only. A market summary that inner-joins labels first silently shrinks the pool whenever a label is missing, which moves every surviving stock's score.

deferred: runs/market-context-441d-s11/armC.* missing: residual liveness is measured on a micro-trained head, not on the delivered weights
wiring.note: If the pipeline hands over a date-only key column, one group covers a whole day and the same-timestamp requirement fails by wiring, not by arithmetic.
